items.q: Mina is holding her red rope. The flashback should start. Which words take the reader back?
opts: Last year, Mina had been given a red rope.
Tomorrow, Mina will be given a red rope.
Mina is given a red rope right now.
items.why: Last year tells the reader we are looking back, and had been given shows it happened before the main story.

items.q: Raj smells satay and remembers something. Which sentence slides into the flashback?
opts: The smell reminded him of the night market. Last year, Dad had bought him a balloon there.
The smell reminded him of the night market. Next week, Dad will buy him a balloon there.
The smell reminded him of the night market. Dad buys him a balloon.
items.why: First a memory clue, then a time word like Last year, then had + verb.

items.q: Which words can start a flashback?
items.why: Long ago, Last year and One summer all point to the past. Right now and In a moment do not.

items.q: Which sentence makes the reader want to go back into the flashback?
opts: Hana looked at the block and remembered the day it chipped.
items.why: A memory clue makes the reader wonder what happened, so they follow Hana back.

items.q: Last year, Ethan ___ a red pencil while the teacher gave the clues.
items.why: Start a flashback in the past perfect: had + the verb. It shows this happened before the main story.

items.q: Dad ___ a balloon for Raj before the crowd came.
items.why: Had + bought is the past perfect. It fits the start of a flashback.

items.q: The flashback is already moving. Then Mina ___ down the road after the rope.
items.why: Once the flashback has started you can use the simple past: chased.

items.q: Which sentence has the wrong verb form?
opts: Dad had gave her a rope.
Dad had given her a rope.
items.why: Had gave is wrong. After had we use the past participle: had given.

items.q: The flashback ends and the main story begins again. Which sentence brings the reader back?
opts: Back in the story, Mina took a deep breath.
Last year, Mina took a deep breath.
Long ago, Mina took a deep breath.
items.why: Back in the story tells the reader we have left the flashback.

items.q: Which sentence shows the character has changed after the flashback?
opts: Now Mina counted her jumps out loud, calm and steady.
Mina had counted her jumps last year.
Mina will count her jumps tomorrow.
items.why: Now brings us back to the main story, and her calm counting shows what she learned.

items.q: Which word helps the reader leave the flashback?
items.why: Now, points to the main story. Long ago and Last year point back to the past.

items.q: Back in the main story, which verb is correct? Raj ___ up to the helper and said his name.
items.why: The main story is told in the simple past, so we return to it with walked.
